course_description:
This course examines visitor psychology in tourism, hospitality and event contexts and focuses on the design and marketing of visitor experiences and environments. Students in the course will analyse visitors' motivations to engage in tourist experiences, visitor decision making, and marketing in tourism, hospitality and event contexts.

Visitor Experience and Design will introduce you to a series of visitor experience design concepts and research approaches. This course will combine perspectives from anthropology, sociology, social psychology, tourism, events, hospitality, consumer behaviour and human geography as a basis for understanding visitor experiences. It will also provide you with an understanding of how an individual's internal factors can result in them making a decision to (or to not) choose a visitor experience.ﾠ

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

Course structure and assessments have been modified to better align with a workplace/ professional scenario and graduate attributes.

assessment_details.title: Visitor Experience Appraisal Vlog
assessment_details.due_date: 28/08/2026 2:00 pm Both vlog and the one-page document are due on the same date, same time.
assessment_details.task_description: Visitor experiences can provide great value; however, they can sometimes be outdated or irrelevant and may fail to attract targeted visitors. New competitors or substitute products may also become available. Therefore, plans need to be continually refreshed to ensure that the visitor experience is competitive and relevant to target markets. Select an experience provider (real) and conduct an appraisal of an existing experience. You will incorporate demographics, geographics, psychographics, and decision-making from a visitor’s perspective to appraise the experience. This must be a recent experience you have had, and you will need photos/videos you took (preferably with you in them) at the site/venue. Visitor Experiences sites can include: A theme park, zoo, aquarium, botanical gardens or cultural attraction An interpretation centre, museum, art gallery, heritage/historic site A winery, brewery, and working farm A festival or event Other (check with your Tutor) Part A You will produce a YouTube-style vlog documenting your visit to and appraisal of a real visitor experience site. The video must be filmed in landscape format, and you must appear on screen. You may record continuously at the site, compile a series of clips and/or photos taken there, or use a combination of both approaches, but all footage and images must be your own and taken during a genuine visit. Your video must cover all four content sections below, in order: Introduction - Briefly introduce the site: its name, location, type of experience, and its current target audience. Show the site on camera and talk the viewer through what they are seeing. Market Segment/s and Motives - Identify and profile the market segment/s you will target with your redesigned experience, applying the segmentation techniques covered in class (demographics, geographics, psychographics, decision-making). Apply one motivation theory or model from the course; do not mix and match models, to explain why your chosen segment would be motivated to engage with the redesigned experience. Need for Redesign - Explain and justify why this experience needs to be redesigned. Use SCEPTICAL factors or other relevant course frameworks. Do not simply list numerous superficial reasons why it should be redesigned. It does not need to be major or revolutionary. It might be about focusing more on a specific market, the need for a new site management procedure, or an updated promotion. Think about what is feasible and would be deemed relevant by both the experience provider and the potential visitors. Conclusion - Summarise why the redesign would benefit the experience provider and why your target segment is the right focus. Speak directly to the camera for this section. Video requirements: Vlog length should be 7-8 minutes. Filmed in landscape (16:9) - vertical/portrait footage will not be accepted You must appear on screen (face visible). All photos and video footage must be your own, taken during a genuine site visit. Background music is optional; if used, ensure it does not obscure your commentary. Video must be submitted to Blackboard via the EchoVideo deep linking tool. Part B Alongside your video, you must submit a single-page professionally formatted summary document. The 1-pager is not a script or transcript; it is a concise, standalone reference document that communicates the essence of your appraisal. A template will be provided on Blackboard to complete this part. The 1-page document must include: Your full name, preferred name, student number, and tutorial group. Site name, location, and type of visitor experience. Your identified target market. A complete APA 7 reference list. A declaration of any AI or MT tools used, with specific instances noted. Submission Submit both the video file and the 1-page PDF/Word document to Blackboard by the due date. Further information will be provided on Blackboard and in Tutorials. assessment_details.title: Visitor Experience Redesign Report
assessment_details.task_description: As the Experience Design Manager of your site, you will now create a redesign proposal based on the feedback and insights gathered in Assessment 1. The proposal should focus on improving the existing experience based on the core concepts from the course, such as the Orchestra Model, Experiencescape, Visitor Management, and Interpretation. You will present a clear and professional plan to enhance visitor engagement, operational efficiency, and overall visitor satisfaction. The proposal should be presented as a formal business document, with a focus on practical, actionable strategies. Your proposal will include an implementation plan, expected outcomes, and a timeline, allowing you to demonstrate both your analytical skills and your ability to think strategically in a business context. The entire report (proposal) should be presented creatively, integrating infographics within the report itself. The visuals should be part of the document to enhance the reader’s understanding and engagement, not as a separate document. You are encouraged to make the proposal visually appealing while maintaining its professional and business-focused structure. (Examples will be provided during the tutorials.) Proposal Structure: Executive Summary Provide a brief summary of the proposal, outlining the current challenges, the proposed changes, and the expected outcomes of the redesign. Introduction to the Site In this section, provide an overview of the site you are redesigning. Include details such as the name, description, location, and current visitor experience. Highlight the target market of the site. Current Visitor Experience and Challenges Analyse the current visitor experience, identifying key challenges (e.g., overcrowding, lack of engagement). Include the Orchestra Model (Current) to explain how the five elements (sensory, affective, cognitive, behavioural, relationships) apply to the current experience. Consider including this as a table. Proposed Redesign Strategy Present the proposed redesign strategy, addressing improvements in: Orchestra Model (Redesign): Focus on one element (sensory, affective, cognitive, behavioural, relationships) to enhance. Experiencescape: Propose physical or environmental changes to improve visitor flow and engagement. (See Bitner, 1992) servicescape- (ambient conditions, spatial layout). Visitor Management: Offer strategies to optimise queues, crowding, and staff interactions. Interpretation: Suggest improvements in how information is shared with visitors (e.g., digital displays, storytelling). Implementation Plan In this section, provide a clear timeline of key milestones for the proposed redesign. Since this is a smaller-scale redesign, the milestones should focus on immediate actions that are achievable within a short to medium timeframe. Post-Experience Outcomes You should also describe how you will evaluate, monitor and improve experience quality and visitor satisfaction. What will you do to encourage repeat business or to develop an ongoing relationship with visitors? How will you help visitors create, share and recall positive memories of their experiences? References A Reference List should be included in APA7 style. As a bare minimum, a pass assignment should contain at least ten (10) references from a variety of sources, including websites, books, reports, journal articles and other sources. Further information will be provided on Blackboard and in Tutorials. Word Count 2000 - 2500 words (+/- 10%) Read full task description Hide full task description

Understanding Visitors: Demographics, Geographics, Behavioural and Psychographics. Understanding the key characteristics of the target market and how to best align visitor experiences for these target markets. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Introduction to Visitor Experience Course orientation and meet your tutors. Activities related to new business environment and trends in experience design. We will also discuss assessment 1 and understand how to conduct an appraisal of an existing experience. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Understanding Visitors: Motivations It is important for managers to understand their visitors, in particular their motives for the visitor experiences they seek. This week will continue to build on our understanding of target markets and learn how to apply motivation theory to visitor experience design. Public Holiday - EKKA - Wednesday, 12/08/2026 - Check Blackboard for announcements regarding rescheduled activity. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Understanding your Target Market Activities related to understanding the characteristics of your target market. This will also help you understand target markets for your assessments. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

Understanding Visitors: Perceptions & Decision Making This week we will understand how all visitors perceive things differently and how these perceptions influence their experience. We will also understand the decision-making process. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

Understanding Visitor Psychographics We will understand the different personality Traits. Students will have an opportunity to undertake a personality test to determine their preferences and traits and how this influences their travel decisions. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Experience Design: Experience Economy & Visitor Journey Understanding the importance of experience economy and visitor journey. Learning outcomes: L01, L03

Understanding Visitor Motivation and Destination Images We will participate in activities to understand visitor motivations, what destinations images are and how they are created. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Experience Design: Orchestra Model By applying the Orchestra Model theory, we will understand how visitor experiences are curated and evaluated holistically. Learning outcomes: L03, L04

Experience Design and Understanding Visitor Journey We will participate in activities to understand the Experience Economy framework. We will also evaluate visitor journey with the help of a powerful tool called the Customer Journey Map (CJM). We will unpack assessment task 2 and conduct a practice session on how to complete this task. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Experience Design: Storytelling We will understand how storytelling is an impactful technique for making meaningful connections with visitors. Learning outcomes: L03, L04

To do this, we will get out of the classroom and explore UQ campus museums and various visitor spaces around the campus. Part of 1 of assessment task 2 will also take place during this tutorial. Learning outcomes: L01, L03

Experience Design: Storytelling We will participate in activities based on storytelling techniques. Get ready to deliver an exciting story in your tutorials. Part of 2 of assessment task 2 will also take place during this tutorial. Learning outcomes: L03
